claims.reason: Absence can be shown only from a whole text. The Gardiner snapshot is an abstract only (Europe PMC); it does not mention individual sensitivity, but the full text of Gardiner et al. would be needed to show absence. The NHS snapshot is the main region (4304 of 4844 chars): searched for sensitiv*, individual, genetic, metabol*, toleran*, habitual, vary/variab*, differ, personal; the only hit is 'Everyone needs different amounts of sleep' (line 37), which concerns sleep need, not caffeine sensitivity. So absence holds for the NHS main region and is undecided for the full text of the meta-analysis.

scope_gaps.note: 'dla wszystkich' can be read as all caffeine sources (the Gardiner abstract gives two different intervals) or all people (no snapshot reports individual differences). Neither snapshot mentions a single clock hour.
The NHS line is general self-help for insomnia and lists smoking and alcohol next to tea and coffee. It gives no dose, no other caffeine sources and no reason or effect size for the 6 hours.

The abstract does not state the population, the doses/timings of the underlying studies, or the confidence interval. The interval is tied only to avoiding a reduction in total sleep time, not to sleep onset, efficiency or deep sleep.
Only an abstract was read: the method by which 8.8 h and 13.2 h were derived from the pooled data is not shown.
The abstract gives no comparator, dose, timing, population or confidence interval for the 45 min figure. A reader might assume a fixed dose or healthy adults; the sentence does not say so.

The two intervals are minimums ('at least') and are tied to avoiding reduced total sleep time only. A reader might assume they protect other sleep measures or all people; the sentence does not say so.
The sentence as a whole names a clock hour (14:00). No snapshot contains 14:00 or any clock-time rule; both give hours before bedtime. The figure 14:00 is therefore not quoted from any source.

The coffee figure is per 250 mL and the supplement figure per standard serve with no volume given, so the two are not like-for-like, and the supplement is not described as a drink. The sentence does not claim a like-for-like comparison.
'Cytowane źródła' covers two cited snapshots: the Gardiner abstract (abstract only) and the NHS page (main region only).
